title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
statement_short: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (i.e., from left to right, level by level).
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in tree <= 2000, -1000 <= Node.val <= 1000
hint: Small node count (<= 2000) permits queue-based breadth-first traversal grouping nodes by level depth.
keywords: left to right, level by level
why_not: Right: Tree BFS uses a queue to collect node values level by level from left to right in O(n) time and O(w) space. Not Tree DFS: Recursive DFS requires passing a level index to append values to sub-lists, whereas BFS visits levels sequentially. Not Stack: LIFO processing reverses node traversal order rather than preserving level order. Not 1D DP: Dynamic programming state caching does not apply to sequential tree level traversal.
